stem:
A star-shaped figure was cut in the black paper strip used for covering the leaf of a destarched plant used for demonstrating that light is necessary for photosynthesis. At the end of the experiment when the leaf was tested for starch with iodine, the star-shaped figure on the leaf was found to be:

(The figure shows a leaf covered by a black paper strip; a star-shaped portion has been cut out of the black paper so that light reaches only the star-shaped region of the leaf.)

In the sketch of the stomatal apparatus given below, which one of the following is missing?

(The figure is a sketch of a stomatal apparatus: two bean-shaped guard cells enclosing a central pore, with chloroplasts shown as dots inside the guard cells and the cell walls and cell membranes outlined; no nuclei are drawn inside the guard cells.)

A star-shaped black paper was used to cover a leaf in a destarched plant as shown below. The plant was left in sunlight for four hours and then the leaf was plucked, black paper removed and tested for the presence of starch. The areas which turned blue-black when iodine solution was added were:

(The figure shows a leaf with a star-shaped black-paper cover over its central part. Region I is the exposed leaf area outside the cover, II is the star-shaped covered region at the centre, while III and IV are exposed leaf regions around the star.)

A destarched leaf on a potted plant was covered with black (A), white (B) and transparent (C) strips of paper as shown in the figure. After six hours of exposure to sunlight the leaf was removed from the plant and tested for starch. Which one of the following will be the correct observation?

(The figure shows one leaf crossed by three vertical strips: strip A is a black/opaque strip, strip B is a white strip, and strip C is a transparent strip; the rest of the leaf is uncovered.)

options.label: A
options.text: Only A and B portions remained colourless and the rest of the leaf turned blue-black

options.label: B
options.text: Only B and C portions turned blue-black

options.label: C
options.text: A, B and C portions remained colourless and the rest of the leaf turned blue-black

stem:
Shown below are four parts of a slide of an epidermal peel, marked I, II, III and IV. Which part out of these four should be focused under high power to view complete stomata?

(The figure is an epidermal-peel slide with four small boxed regions labelled I, II, III and IV; the boxes highlight different patches of the peel, only one of which contains a complete stoma — two guard cells enclosing a pore.)

A student had drawn the diagram of stomata as shown below in a hurry. He could not be given full marks as he:

(The figure is a roughly drawn stomata diagram: the two guard cells around the central pore show a few dots but the chloroplasts are not clearly drawn, and the surrounding epidermal cells have no nuclei drawn in them.)

options.label: A
options.text: did not draw nuclei in guard cells and other cells

options.label: B
options.text: did not label the stoma in its correct position

options.label: C
options.text: should have drawn nuclei and chloroplasts in guard cells and nuclei in all epidermal cells

options.label: D
options.text: forgot to draw nuclei in guard cells and also to label the diagram

stem:
An experimental set-up is given below to demonstrate that CO₂ is given out during respiration. Four students made the following observations marked I, II, III and IV:

1. Level of water remained the same in both the beaker and the delivery tube
2. Level of water increased in the delivery tube
3. Level of water gets reduced in both the beaker and the delivery tube
4. Water ascends into the delivery tube and back flows into the beaker

Which one of the above is the correct observation?

(The figure is a conical flask closed with a rubber cork holding germinating seeds at the bottom; a small test tube of KOH solution hangs inside by a thread, and a glass delivery tube runs from the flask down into a beaker of water.)

A student performed the starch test on a leaf. Some steps involved are shown below. The correct sequence of steps should be:

(The figure shows four steps: (i) leaf in boiling water heated over a flame, (ii) leaf in iodine solution, (iii) leaf in ethanol heated in a water bath, and (iv) leaf in water at room temperature.)

Out of the four experimental set-ups shown below, which one will demonstrate the evolution of carbon dioxide during respiration of germinating seeds?

(The figure shows four flask set-ups: I — a flask closed with a cotton plug, holding germinating seeds and a small tube of KOH solution, connected to a beaker of water; II — a flask closed with a rubber cork, holding KOH solution but no germinating seeds, connected to water; III — a flask closed with a rubber cork, holding germinating seeds but no KOH, connected to water; IV — a flask closed with a rubber cork, holding germinating seeds and a tube of KOH solution, connected to a beaker of water.)

Which statement is correct for the following image?

(The figure shows sunlight falling on a green leaf whose central part is covered by a black-paper strip, so that the covered region receives no light.)

options.label: B
options.text: Sunlight is not essential for chlorophyll

options.label: C
options.text: Sunlight is not essential for photosynthesis

stem:
Four students use the experimental set-up shown above. The set-up that would show that "carbon dioxide is given out during respiration" is:

(The figure shows four set-ups: I — a potted plant enclosed under a bell jar with a cork sealing, showing water droplets on the inside; II — a Hydrilla plant in a beaker of water with sodium bicarbonate, a funnel and an inverted test tube collecting oxygen bubbles; III — a freshly plucked leaf partly covered with black paper; IV — a conical flask of germinating seeds with a small test tube of KOH solution, connected by a delivery tube to a beaker of water marked with the initial level.)

Which structure out of I, II, III and IV marked in the given diagram of the epidermal peel of leaf should be labelled as stoma?

(The figure is an epidermal peel showing a pair of guard cells enclosing a central pore; arrows I, II, III and IV point respectively to a guard cell, to the central pore between the guard cells, to a guard-cell wall and to a surrounding epidermal cell.)

The diagram below is the experimental set-up to show that carbon dioxide is given out during respiration. In this set-up what does the test tube marked (X) contain?

(The figure is a conical flask connected by a delivery tube to a beaker; a small test tube marked (X) hangs inside the flask.)

In the experimental set-up shown below, KOH solution has been kept in the flask to:

(The figure is a flask closed with a rubber cork, holding germinating seeds at the bottom and a small tube of KOH solution, connected by a delivery tube to a beaker of water.)

options.label: A
options.text: absorb carbon dioxide so as to create a partial vacuum

options.label: B
options.text: react with water to generate oxygen

options.label: C
options.text: remove impurities present in the air in the flask

options.label: D
options.text: create a dry atmosphere for wet germinating seeds

stem:
In the diagram of the stomatal pore given below, the marking corresponding to the chloroplast is:

(The figure shows two guard cells enclosing a pore; arrow A points to a guard cell, B points to a small dot inside a guard cell, C points to a large dark oval body inside a guard cell, and D points to a lower part of the guard cell.)

In the above experiment (a flask of germinating seeds with KOH connected to a tube of water), water will rise in the tube because:

1. oxygen of air in the flask will be taken up by the germinating seeds
2. carbon dioxide given out by the germinating seeds will be absorbed by KOH
3. carbon dioxide given out will go through the glass tube and push water up into the tube
4. moisture in the germinating seeds will reach the water in the beaker through the delivery tube

The correct reason of water to rise in the tube is:

In the following diagram, identify the cells through which massive amounts of gaseous exchange takes place for photosynthesis:

(The figure is a vertical section of a leaf: I is the upper epidermis, II is the elongated palisade mesophyll, III is the loosely packed spongy mesophyll, and IV is the lower epidermis bearing a stoma, indicated by an arrow.)

The figure which does not illustrate any of the steps of the experiment to show that light is necessary for photosynthesis is:

(The figure shows steps labelled I, II, III, and a step IV is referred to in the options: I — a leaf partly covered with a paper strip; II — a leaf in a beaker of liquid being heated over a flame on a tripod; III — a leaf in a beaker being heated directly over a flame on a tripod.)

The following experiment was set-up to show that gas is given out during respiration. But there was no rise in the level of water. This was because:

(The figure shows a flask closed with a rubber cork, holding germinating seeds, connected by a delivery tube to a beaker of water; no KOH or other absorbing substance is present in the flask.)

options.label: A
options.text: no substance is kept in the flask to absorb the gas given out by the seeds

options.label: B
options.text: germinating seeds have not been kept under water in the flask

options.label: C
options.text: water is kept in the beaker instead of limewater

options.label: D
options.text: the cork on the flask is made of rubber

stem:
The germinating seeds present in the experimental set-up shown below:

(The figure is a flask closed with a rubber cork, holding germinating seeds and a small tube of KOH, connected by a delivery tube to a beaker of water.)

options.label: A
options.text: take up CO₂ from the atmosphere

options.label: B
options.text: take up O₂ from the water

options.label: C
options.text: release CO₂ into the air in the flask

stem:
Students observed the epidermal peel of a leaf under the high power of a microscope. The following are the sketches made by them. The correct sketch is:

The four option sketches of a stomatal apparatus are:
- A: two guard cells around a pore drawn as plain outlines, with no chloroplasts or nuclei shown.
- B: two guard cells around a pore, each containing several chloroplasts (small dots) and a distinct nucleus, surrounded by epidermal cells.
- C: two guard cells with a few scattered dots but no clear nuclei.
- D: two guard cells with dots and large dark nuclei but the surrounding cells incomplete.

A leaf from a destarched plant is covered with a black paper strip across its middle as shown in figure 1. The starch test is done on the leaf after 8 hours. The result will be as shown in diagram:

In figure 1 the black paper covers only the middle band of the leaf, so after the starch test the covered middle stays white (no starch) while the uncovered top and bottom turn blue-black. The four result diagrams are:
- A: top White, middle Blue-black, bottom White.
- B: top Blue-black, middle White, bottom Blue-black.
- C: top Blue-black, middle Green, bottom Blue-black.
- D: top White, middle Green, bottom White.

After performing the experiment to show that germinating seeds give out carbon dioxide during respiration, students drew the following diagrams. The correct labelled diagram is:

Each option is a flask connected by a delivery tube to a beaker:
- A: Dry gram seeds, KOH, beaker of Water.
- B: Boiled gram seeds, KOH, beaker of Lime water.
- C: Germinating gram seeds, KOH, beaker of Water.
- D: Wet and germinating gram seeds, no KOH, beaker of Water.

In the following diagram of the stomatal apparatus, which parts are incorrectly labelled?

(The figure is a stomatal apparatus with five labels: (I) Guard cell, (II) Chloroplast, (III) Cell wall of stomata, (IV) Stomata and (V) Epidermal cell, each pointing to a part of the diagram.)

Observe the following diagram and identify the process and its significance from the following options:

(The figure shows a tree absorbing water through its roots, the water moving up the stem shown by upward arrows, and water vapour escaping from the leaf.)

options.label: A
options.text: Translocation: helps in transporting materials from one cell to another

options.label: B
options.text: Excretion: helps in excreting out waste water from the plant

options.label: C
options.text: Evaporation: maintains water contents in leaf cells

options.label: D
options.text: Transpiration: creates a suction force which pulls water inside the plant

stem:
Which part of the leaf will have starch when exposed to sunlight?

(The figure shows a leaf crossed by a strip of opaque paper over its middle; B is the uncovered region above the strip, C is the region covered by the strip, and A is the uncovered region below the strip.)

In order to complete the diagram of stomatal apparatus given below, nuclei should be drawn in the parts marked:

(The figure is an incomplete stomatal apparatus where arrow A points to the central pore, arrow B points to a guard cell and arrow C points to a surrounding epidermal cell.)

In an experiment on photosynthesis, students were instructed to cover a portion of a leaf of a destarched potted plant with opaque paper as shown in the figure. "A" covered one of the leaves with a red strip, "B" with green, "C" with blue and "D" with black. When the starch test was done on the leaves after 4 hours, the result showed no starch in:

(The figure shows four leaves A, B, C and D, each crossed by a coloured strip — red, green, blue and black respectively.)

options.label: B
options.text: the portion covered with black and blue strips

options.label: C
options.text: the portion covered with red, green and blue strips

options.label: D
options.text: the portion covered with green strips

stem:
Given below are two columns, Column I shows enzymes secreted by the glands in the alimentary canal of human beings and Column II indicates the components of food on which enzymes act. Choose the option showing correct matching:

| | Column I (Enzymes) | Column II (Component) |
|---|---|---|
| (a) | Pepsin | Starch |
| (b) | Trypsin | Proteins |
| (c) | Lipase | Proteins |
| (d) | Amylase | Emulsified fat |

Match the following with correct response.

| Column A | Column B |
|---|---|
| (i) Insects | (a) Gills |
| (ii) Earthworm | (b) Trachea |
| (iii) Fishes | (c) Lungs |
| (iv) Mammals | (d) Skin |

Match the following with correct response.

| Column A | Column B |
|---|---|
| (i) Pulmonary artery | (a) Oxygenated blood |
| (ii) Pulmonary vein | (b) Exchange of substances |
| (iii) Aorta | (c) Supplies blood to body tissues/parts |
| (iv) Capillary | (d) Deoxygenated blood |

Match the following with correct response.

| Column A | Column B |
|---|---|
| (i) Saliva | (a) Sucrose |
| (ii) Gastric juice | (b) Pepsin |
| (iii) Pancreatic juice | (c) Amylase |
| (iv) Succus entericus | (d) Trypsin |

Match the following with correct response.

| Column A | Column B |
|---|---|
| (i) Epiglottis | (a) Blood coagulation |
| (ii) Platelets | (b) Sphygmomanometer |
| (iii) An instrument used to check normal activities of the heart | (c) Electrocardiograph |
| (iv) An instrument used to measure the blood pressure of the human heart | (d) Covers wind pipe while swallowing food |

Match the following with correct response.

| Column A | Column B |
|---|---|
| (i) The red colour of human blood | (a) Chlorophyll |
| (ii) The pigment which absorbs solar energy | (b) Liver |
| (iii) The largest gland of the human body | (c) Liver |
| (iv) Pumping organ of the body | (d) Haemoglobin |
In grasshopper, gaseous exchange takes place through ______.
Conversion of milk to curds is due to ______.

Given below are randomly written steps for the experiments to show that light is necessary for photosynthesis. What out of the following is the correct sequence of steps for a successful run of the experiment?
1. Pluck the experimental leaf
2. Using strips of black paper, cover a portion of the leaf on both sides
3. De-starch leaf of the potted plant
4. Test the experimental leaf for the presence of starch
5. Expose the plant to sunlight for four hours
6. Remove the black paper strips from the leaf

The steps involved in making a slide of the epidermal peel of leaf are given as follows:
1. Pull out a thin peel from the lower surface of the leaf.
2. Put a drop of glycerine on the slide.
3. Stain the peel in safranin.
4. Place the stained peel of the glycerine.
5. Place the coverslip over the peel.
Which one is the correct sequence of steps to be followed?

Which of the following statement(s) is (are) true about human heart?
1. Right atrium receives oxygenated blood from lungs through pulmonary artery.
2. Left atrium transfers oxygenated blood to left ventricle which sends it in various parts of the body.
3. Right atrium receives deoxygenated blood through vena cava from upper and lower body.
4. Left atrium transfers oxygenated blood to aorta which sends it to different parts of the body.

A stomata closes when:
1. It needs carbon dioxide for photosynthesis.
2. It does not need carbon dioxide for photosynthesis.
3. Water flows out of the guard cells.
4. Water flows into the guard cells.
The correct response(s) in this process is/are:
Choose the correct statement that describes arteries.

options.label: A
options.text: They have thick elastic walls, blood flows under high pressure; collect blood from different organs and bring it back to the heart

options.label: B
options.text: They have thick elastic walls, blood flows under low pressure; carry blood from different organs of the body

options.label: C
options.text: They have thick elastic walls without valves inside, blood flows under high pressure and carry blood away from the heart to different parts of the body

options.label: D
options.text: They have thin walls with valves inside, blood flows under low pressure and carry blood away from the heart to various organs of the body

stem: Which of the following is the correct statement regarding bile?

options.label: A
options.text: Secreted by bile duct and stored in liver

options.label: B
options.text: Secreted by gall bladder and stored in liver

options.label: C
options.text: Secreted by liver and stored in bile duct

options.label: D
options.text: Secreted by liver and stored in gall bladder

stem: Which of the following statements about the autotrophs is incorrect?

options.label: A
options.text: They convert CO₂ and water into carbohydrates in the absence of sunlight

options.label: B
options.text: They store carbohydrates in the form of starch

options.label: C
options.text: They constitute the first trophic level in food chains

options.label: D
options.text: They synthesize carbohydrates from CO₂ and water in the presence of sunlight & chlorophyll

stem:
Which of the following statement(s) is (are) correct?
1. Pyruvate can be converted into ethanol and carbon dioxide by yeast
2. Fermentation takes place in aerobic bacteria
3. Fermentation takes place in mitochondria
4. Fermentation is a form of anaerobic respiration
Select the correct statement

options.label: A
options.text: Heterotrophs do not synthesise their own food

options.label: C
options.text: Heterotrophs are capable of converting carbon dioxide and water into carbohydrates

options.label: D
options.text: Heterotrophs utilise solar energy for photosynthesis

stem: Which one of the following statements is correct about the human circulatory system?

options.label: A
options.text: Blood transports only oxygen and not carbon dioxide.

options.label: C
options.text: Both oxygen-rich and oxygen-deficient blood gets mixed in the heart.

options.label: D
options.text: Valves ensure that the blood does not flow backwards.

stem:
Which of the following statement (s) is (are) true about the heart?
1. The left atrium receives oxygenated blood from different parts of the body while the right atrium receives deoxygenated blood from lungs
2. The left ventricle pumps oxygenated blood to different body parts while right ventricle pumps deoxygenated blood to lungs
3. Left atrium transfers oxygenated blood to the right ventricle which sends it to different parts of the body
4. Right atrium receives deoxygenated blood from different parts of the body while left ventricle pumps oxygenated blood to different parts of the body
Select from the following the correct statement about tropic movement in plants:

options.label: A
options.text: It is a growth related movement.

options.label: B
options.text: It does not depend on the direction of stimulus received.

options.label: C
options.text: It is due to stimulus of touch and temperature.

options.label: D
options.text: It is independent of any stimulus.

stem: Consider the following statements about small intestine and select the one which is NOT correct:

options.label: A
options.text: The villi of the small intestine absorb water from the unabsorbed food before it gets removed from the body via the anus.

options.label: B
options.text: The small intestine is the site of complete digestion of food.

options.label: C
options.text: The small intestine receives secretions from liver and pancreas.

options.label: D
options.text: The length of the small intestine in animals differs as it depends on the type of food they eat.

stem: Which of the following is an incorrect statement?

options.label: A
options.text: Energy is essential for life processes

options.label: B
options.text: Movement of molecules does not take place among cells

options.label: D
options.text: Organisms must repair and maintain their structure

stem:
Which of the following statement(s) is (are) true about respiration?
1. During inhalation, ribs move inward and the diaphragm is raised
2. In the alveoli, exchange of gases takes place i.e., oxygen from alveolar air diffuses into blood and carbon dioxide from the blood into the alveolar air
3. Haemoglobin has a greater affinity for carbon dioxide than oxygen
4. Alveoli increase surface area for exchange of gases
